subject: Post-call: technical qualification & latency/throughput targets for ZenithAI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zenithai.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput targets

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Below is a quick recap of the pain we heard, the measurable goals you described, and the recommended next steps we discussed on the call. I want to make sure we captured everything before we schedule the technical deep dive with our solutions + security team.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Latency spikes under peak: interactive user experience is inconsistent, especially for autocomplete/chat flows.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic surges (bursty usage from web UI + API).
- Need to support multi-turn retrieval-augmented generation with per-request context up to ~2k tokens.
- Compliance: customer PII must never leave our US region and audit logs retained for 1 year.

Stated goals / success metrics (what you told us)
- P95 latency target: < 350 ms for typical 256-token responses (single-turn) under normal load.
- Peak concurrency: 100–150 concurrent interactive sessions; expected peak of ~250 reqs/minute during events.
- Sustained throughput target: ~300 tokens/sec aggregated across the service.
- Quality: want to evaluate Mistral- or Llama-series 7–13B variants; cost target to be <X per 1k tokens (we'll estimate).

Key technical constraints
- Data residency: US-only, must be auditable (SOC2 evidence and request logs).
- Retrieval augmentation: vector DB calls per request (avg 3–5 external lookups); prefix/KV caching could reduce compute.
- Retry/fallback behavior for model failures required.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) I'll attach the load profile you said you'd share and a short topology draft — can you confirm the load CSV is the most current? (Attachment: zenithai-load-profile.csv)
2) Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop next week with Ethan (solutions eng) and Neha (security) to walk the proposed Dedicated/private options and deep-dive into SLOs and quantization tradeoffs.
3) We'll produce a short SLO matrix and two deployment options (Dedicated pool vs Private VPC) and an initial cost estimate for the pilot.

Proposed times for workshop (PST):
- Tue 9/15 10:00–11:30
- Wed 9/16 14:00–15:30

If the times above don't work let me know alternatives.

Thanks — I pulled a few quick thoughts for the workshop: potential for KV caching to cover repeated prefix prompts; a canary rollout with automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant during capacity pressure; and a batching window target we can tune to balance latency and unit cost.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
[Attachment: zenithai-load-profile.csv (csv)]
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zenithai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenithai.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput targets

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few details and adding clarifications from our side:

Clarifications:
- P95 target: we agreed to aim for <350ms for single-turn 256-token median responses; for multi-turn with retrieval (avg 3 lookups) we'd accept up to ~800ms as long as 95th stays below 1s.
- Peak behavior: our previous spikes came from batched UX events, so we need graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or cached responses).

Model preferences and constraints:
- Preference to test Mistral-7B quantized first for cost reasons, but we'll want to benchmark Llama-3/13B-range for higher-quality outputs on the most important flows.
- Must support token limits up to 2k in the short term.

Security/compliance reminders:
- All inference logs must be retained and searchable for 12 months.
- We will need an inventory of the logs Redwood stores and exact retention configuration for the pilot.

I've attached a sanitized load profile (zenithai-load-profile.csv) — that should show the request rate distribution and event spikes we saw in July.

We're good on the workshop; Tue 9/15 10:00–11:30 works for Priya and me. Please include an agenda and pre-reads if you can.

—Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Engineering, Zenith AI
alex.kim@zenithai.com | +1 (650) 555-0189
[Attachment: zenithai-load-profile.csv (csv)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zenithai.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput targets

Thanks Alex — attaching a short topology sketch and an initial SLO matrix for the workshop. Quick notes below so Ethan/Neha can prep.

Recommended pilot approach (high level)
- Option A: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) — 2 x A100 equivalents to start, autoscale to 4 on sustained traffic; canary rollout across model variants; recommended batching target 10–25 ms to preserve p95 while improving throughput.
- Option B: Private (VPC) — private control plane, customer-managed VPC peering; good when you need strict network isolation and HSM/KMS integration for keys.

Runtime / infra notes
- Model variants: Mistral-7B quantized as baseline + Llama-3-13B as high-quality variant. Runtime will use prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts and dynamic batching per route.
- Throughput: given the CSV, we estimate needing ability to sustain ~300 tokens/sec with burst capacity to 1k tokens/sec for short windows; this maps to ~2 dedicated A100s for Mistral baseline with caching, or 3–4 for the larger Llama variant depending on quantization.
- SLOs: we'll draft a matrix for the workshop (p50/p95/p99 latency for single-turn vs RAG flows).

Security & compliance checklist (for Neha)
- Confirm log locations, retention settings (12 months), and what will be in the audit bundle for SOC2 review.
- Data residency: confirm US-only routing and keys.

Attachments included:
- proposed-topology-diagram.png (diagram showing Dedicated vs Private with caching layer)
- rough SLO matrix (included inline in the workshop pre-read doc in Drive link)

Agenda for Tue 9/15 10:00–11:30 (PST)
1) 10m intro + goals
2) 30m load profile & performance expectations (Ethan)
3) 30m deployment/topology & cost tradeoffs (Marissa + Ethan)
4) 20m security/compliance checklist (Neha)
5) 10m next steps & pilot proposal

I'll send a calendar invite and pre-reads (Drive link) shortly.

Cheers,

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput targets

Perfect — thanks. Calendar invite confirmed. A couple of small asks before the workshop:
- Can you include a short cost estimate for both pilot options (Dedicated vs Private) in the pre-read? We want a ballpark to share with finance ahead of time.
- Please add sample SLA language or uptime commitments we can reference (even draft).
- I'll upload a signed NDA (attached) and add a pre-authorization for a limited pilot so we can run load tests with production-like traffic.

Attached: NDA (nda-zenithai.pdf). See you Tue.

Alex
